12.24.s: ata ūrdhvam daśa āhanasyāḥ | yad devāso lalāmagum pra viṣṭīminam āviṣuḥ | sakthnā dediśyate nārī satyasya akṣibhuvo yathā | yad asyā aṃhu bhedyāḥ kṛdhu sthūlam upātasat | muṣkāv id asyā ejato go śaphe śakulāv iva | yadā sthūlena pasasāṇau muṣkā upāvadhīt | viṣvañcāv asyā vardhataḥ sikatāv iva gardabhau | mahānagnī mahānagnam dhāvantam anu dhāvati | imās tu tasya gā rakṣa yabha mām addhy odanam | mahānagnī kṛkavākum śamyayā pari dhāvati | vayam na vidma yo mṛgaḥ śīrṣṇā harati dhāṇikām | mahānagny upa brūte svasty āveśitam pasaḥ | ittham phalasya vṛkṣasya śūrpam śūrpam bhajemahi | mahānagny ulūkhalam atikrāmanty abravīt | yathā tava vanaspate ni ghnanti tathā mama | mahān vai bhadro bilvo mahān bhadra udumbaraḥ | mahān abhijñu bādhate mahataḥ sādhu khodanam |
12.24.d: अत ऊर्ध्वम् दश आहनस्याः । यद् देवासो ललामगुम् प्र विष्टीमिनम् आविषुः । सक्थ्ना देदिश्यते नारी सत्यस्य अक्षिभुवो यथा । यद् अस्या अंहु भेद्याः कृधु स्थूलम् उपातसत् । मुष्काव् इद् अस्या एजतो गो शफे शकुलाव् इव । यदा स्थूलेन पससाणौ मुष्का उपावधीत् । विष्वञ्चाव् अस्या वर्धतः सिकताव् इव गर्दभौ । महानग्नी महानग्नम् धावन्तम् अनु धावति । इमास् तु तस्य गा रक्ष यभ माम् अद्ध्य् ओदनम् । महानग्नी कृकवाकुम् शम्यया परि धावति । वयम् न विद्म यो मृगः शीर्ष्णा हरति धाणिकाम् । महानग्न्य् उप ब्रूते स्वस्त्य् आवेशितम् पसः । इत्थम् फलस्य वृक्षस्य शूर्पम् शूर्पम् भजेमहि । महानग्न्य् उलूखलम् अतिक्रामन्त्य् अब्रवीत् । यथा तव वनस्पते नि घ्नन्ति तथा मम । महान् वै भद्रो बिल्वो महान् भद्र उदुम्बरः । महान् अभिज्ञु बाधते महतः साधु खोदनम् ।
12.24.m:
Hereafter are the ten āhanasyā verses.

When the gods penetrated the spotted, dripping [organ], / the woman is pointed out by her thigh, like an eye-witness of the truth.

When the short and thick [organ] reached her narrow cleft, / her two testicles shake, like two fish in a cow’s hoof-print.

When with the thick penis he struck at the two testicles, / her two [thighs] spread wide apart, like two donkeys in the sand.

The stark-naked woman runs after the stark-naked man as he runs: / ‘Protect these cows of his; have sex with me; eat the boiled rice!’

The stark-naked woman runs around the rooster with a yoke-pin: / ‘We do not know which beast carries the vessel with its head.’

The stark-naked woman addresses the penis that has entered happily: / ‘Thus of the fruit-bearing tree may we receive winnowing basket by winnowing basket.’

The stark-naked woman said as she stepped over the mortar: / ‘Just as they pound down into you, O lord of the forest, so [they do] into me.’

‘Great indeed and auspicious is the bilva tree; great and auspicious is the udumbara; / great, it presses knee-deep; good is the thrusting of the great one.’

12.24.s: kapṛn naro yaddha prācīr iti dve |
12.24.d: कपृन् नरो यद्ध प्राचीर् इति द्वे ।
12.24.m: There are two verses: ‘kapṛn naro’ and ‘yaddha prācīḥ’.

12.24.s: tāsām tṛtīye pāde nyūṅkho yathā vṛṣākapau |
12.24.d: तासाम् तृतीये पादे न्यूङ्खो यथा वृषाकपौ ।
12.24.m: In the third pāda of these there is a nyūṅkha chanting, as in the Vṛṣākapi hymn.

12.24.s: kapṛn nara iti dvitīya daśamayor akṣarayoḥ |
12.24.d: कपृन् नर इति द्वितीय दशमयोर् अक्षरयोः ।
12.24.m: In ‘kapṛn naraḥ’, [it occurs] on the second and tenth syllables.

12.24.s: nyūṅkhena itarāsām avasāya saṃtānāya uttamam padam |
12.24.d: न्यूङ्खेन इतरासाम् अवसाय संतानाय उत्तमम् पदम् ।
12.24.m: Having paused on the other [verses] with the nyūṅkha, the final pāda is [recited] for continuity.

12.24.s: vi i i ī kim ayam idam āho o othā modaiva iti prtigṛṇāti |
12.24.d: वि इ इ ई किम् अयम् इदम् आहो ओ ओथा मोदैव इति प्र्तिगृणाति ।
12.24.m: He responds with: ‘vi i i ī3! Did he say this? o3 othā moda iva!’

12.25.s: sutāso madhumattamāḥ pra maṃhiṣṭhāya yo adribhid ava drapsa iti tṛcāni ṣaṣṭhe |
12.25.d: सुतासो मधुमत्तमाः प्र मंहिष्ठाय यो अद्रिभिद् अव द्रप्स इति तृचानि षष्ठे ।
12.25.m: On the sixth [day] there are triplets: ‘sutāso madhumattamāḥ’, ‘pra maṃhiṣṭhāya’, ‘yo adribhit’, and ‘ava drapsaḥ’.

12.25.s: tvam na indrā bhara tad indra ava ā bhara iti stotriya anurūpau |
12.25.d: त्वम् न इन्द्रा भर तद् इन्द्र अव आ भर इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ ।
12.25.m: ‘tvam na indrā bhara’ and ‘tad indra ava ā bhara’ are the stotriya and anurūpa.
The entire hymn to the most generous one (pra maṃhiṣṭhāya) is [used] on the first Chandoma day.

12.25.s: ā indra no gadhyed u madhvo madintaram iti madhye |
12.25.d: आ इन्द्र नो गध्येद् उ मध्वो मदिन्तरम् इति मध्ये ।
12.25.m: In the middle [is the hymn]: ‘ā indra no gadhyed u madhvo madintaram’.

12.25.s: eto nv indram stavāma sakhāya ity uttame |
12.25.d: एतो न्व् इन्द्रम् स्तवाम सखाय इत्य् उत्तमे ।
12.25.m: On the last [Chandoma day is the hymn]: ‘eto nv indram stavāma sakhāyaḥ’.

12.26.s: indram viśvā indram īśānam ojasā iti stotriya anurūpāv anurūpasya ye pūrve te uttare |
12.26.d: इन्द्रम् विश्वा इन्द्रम् ईशानम् ओजसा इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपाव् अनुरूपस्य ये पूर्वे ते उत्तरे ।
12.26.m: ‘indram viśvāḥ’ and ‘indram īśānam ojasā’ are the stotriya and anurūpa; those that were preceding for the anurūpa become the following.

12.26.s: nū marta ity acchāvākasya aindrād anantaram dvitīya caturthayoḥ prathama uttamayoś ca chandomayoḥ |
12.26.d: नू मर्त इत्य् अच्छावाकस्य ऐन्द्राद् अनन्तरम् द्वितीय चतुर्थयोः प्रथम उत्तमयोश् च छन्दोमयोः ।
12.26.m: The hymn ‘nū martam’ is for the Acchāvāka priest immediately after the Indra hymn on the second and fourth [days] and on the first and last Chandoma days.

12.26.s: viṣṇor nu kam iti itareṣu |
12.26.d: विष्णोर् नु कम् इति इतरेषु ।
12.26.m: On the other days, [it is the hymn] ‘viṣṇor nu kam’.

12.26.s: urum yajñāya iti tṛcam pūrvam sarvatra paryāsāt |
12.26.d: उरुम् यज्ञाय इति तृचम् पूर्वम् सर्वत्र पर्यासात् ।
12.26.m: Everywhere the triplet ‘urum yajñāya’ is placed prior to the concluding stanza.

12.26.s: sam vām karmaṇā iti sadā paryāsaḥ |
12.26.d: सम् वाम् कर्मणा इति सदा पर्यासः ।
12.26.m: The verse ‘sam vām karmaṇā’ is always the concluding stanza.

12.26.s: śrudhī havam hiraścyā āśrut karṇa iti stotriya anurūpau tṛtīye |
12.26.d: श्रुधी हवम् हिरश्च्या आश्रुत् कर्ण इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ तृतीये ।
12.26.m: ‘śrudhī havam’ and ‘hiraścyā āśrutkarṇa’ are the stotriya and anurūpa on the third [day].

12.26.s: imam indra sutam piba pibā somam madāya kam iti caturthe |
12.26.d: इमम् इन्द्र सुतम् पिब पिबा सोमम् मदाय कम् इति चतुर्थे ।
12.26.m: On the fourth [day, they are]: ‘imam indra sutam piba’ and ‘pibā somam madāya kam’.

12.26.s: asāvi soma indra ta imam indra sutam piba iti pañcame |
12.26.d: असावि सोम इन्द्र त इमम् इन्द्र सुतम् पिब इति पञ्चमे ।
12.26.m: On the fifth [day, they are]: ‘asāvi soma indra te’ and ‘imam indra sutam piba’.

12.26.s: pra va indrāya vṛtrahantamāya viśvato dāvann iti ṣaṣṭhe |
12.26.d: प्र व इन्द्राय वृत्रहन्तमाय विश्वतो दावन्न् इति षष्ठे ।
12.26.m: On the sixth [day, they are]: ‘pra va indrāya vṛtrahantamāya’ and ‘viśvato dāvan’.

12.26.s: evayāmarutam śastvā yathā vṛṣākapim |
12.26.d: एवयामरुतम् शस्त्वा यथा वृषाकपिम् ।
12.26.m: Having recited the Evayāmarut hymn just as the Vṛṣākapi hymn,

12.26.s: iha mado iti vairāja nyūṅkham uktvā made mador madasya madirasya madaivo o othā modaiva iti pratigṛṇāti |
12.26.d: इह मदो इति वैराज न्यूङ्खम् उक्त्वा मदे मदोर् मदस्य मदिरस्य मदैवो ओ ओथा मोदैव इति प्रतिगृणाति ।
12.26.m: having uttered the Vairāja-nyūṅkha: ‘iha mado3!’, he responds with: ‘made mador madasya madirasya madaivo3 o3 othā moda iva’.

12.26.s: ṛtur janitrī |
12.26.d: ऋतुर् जनित्री ।

12.26.s: tam asya dyāvā pṛthivī |
12.26.d: तम् अस्य द्यावा पृथिवी ।

12.26.s: viṣṇor nu kam |
12.26.d: विष्णोर् नु कम् ।

12.26.s: pra vaḥ pāntam andhasaḥ |
12.26.d: प्र वः पान्तम् अन्धसः ।
12.26.m: "Forward for you the draught of the soma juice..." [RV 10.30].

12.26.s: chandomeṣu ca |
12.26.d: छन्दोमेषु च ।

12.26.s: tisras tu prathame |
12.26.d: तिस्रस् तु प्रथमे ।

12.26.s: bhavā mitra iti tṛcāc ca pūrvam uttarayoś chandomayoḥ |
12.26.d: भवा मित्र इति तृचाच् च पूर्वम् उत्तरयोश् छन्दोमयोः ।
12.26.m: And before the triplet "Be a friend..." [RV 6.47.8–10] on the latter two Chandoma days.

12.26.s: nū martaḥ paro mātrayā ity uttamām uddhṛtya ṣaṣṭhe |
12.26.d: नू मर्तः परो मात्रया इत्य् उत्तमाम् उद्धृत्य षष्ठे ।
12.26.m: Having removed the last [verse] of "Now a mortal... beyond measure..." [RV 7.99], on the sixth [day].

12.26.s: yad indra citra yad indra te catasra iti stotriya anurūpau prathame chandome |
12.26.d: यद् इन्द्र चित्र यद् इन्द्र ते चतस्र इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ प्रथमे छन्दोमे ।
12.26.m: "Whatever, O Indra, wonderful..." [RV 8.13.12] and "Whatever, O Indra, your four..." [RV 8.13.13] are the stotriya and anurūpa triplets on the first Chandoma day.

12.26.s: purām bhindur iti madhyame | pūrvas tṛco anurūpas tṛtīyā tu prathamā |
12.26.d: पुराम् भिन्दुर् इति मध्यमे । पूर्वस् तृचो अनुरूपस् तृतीया तु प्रथमा ।
12.26.m: "Breaker of strongholds..." [RV 8.61.10] on the middle [Chandoma day]; the preceding triplet is the anurūpa, but the third [verse] is the first.

12.26.s: gāyanti tvā ity uttame |
12.26.d: गायन्ति त्वा इत्य् उत्तमे ।

12.27.m: On the twenty-fourth day, the śastra of all [priests] is [taken] from the first Chandoma day.

12.27.s: yac caturṇām dvitīya prabhṛtīnām tac caturṇām ābhiplavikānām |
12.27.d: यच् चतुर्णाम् द्वितीय प्रभृतीनाम् तच् चतुर्णाम् आभिप्लविकानाम् ।
12.27.m: Whatever belongs to the four [days] beginning with the second belongs to the four Abhiplava days.
From those beginning with the third on the Svarasāman days.

12.27.s: atha yady abhijitam viṣuvantam bṛhat pṛṣṭham viśvajitam mahā vratīyam ahar ity ukthyāni kuryuś cāturviṃśikāny ukthāni |
12.27.d: अथ यद्य् अभिजितम् विषुवन्तम् बृहत् पृष्ठम् विश्वजितम् महा व्रतीयम् अहर् इत्य् उक्थ्यानि कुर्युश् चातुर्विंशिकान्य् उक्थानि ।
12.27.m: Now, if they should make the Abhijit, the Viṣuvant, the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha, the Viśvajit, and the Mahāvrata day into Ukthya days, the ukthas should be those of the twenty-fourth day.

12.27.s: atha yadi pṛṣṭhya abhiplavayoḥ prathame ahanī daśamam ahar ity ukthyāni kuryur aikāhikāny ukthāni |
12.27.d: अथ यदि पृष्ठ्य अभिप्लवयोः प्रथमे अहनी दशमम् अहर् इत्य् उक्थ्यानि कुर्युर् ऐकाहिकान्य् उक्थानि ।
12.27.m: Now, if they should make the first days of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava [six-day periods] and the tenth day into Ukthya days, the ukthas should be those of a one-day sacrifice.

12.27.s: uttamam ābhiplavikam ukthyam kuryur yad dvitīyasya ahnas tṛtīya savanam tṛtīya savanam |
12.27.d: उत्तमम् आभिप्लविकम् उक्थ्यम् कुर्युर् यद् द्वितीयस्य अह्नस् तृतीय सवनम् तृतीय सवनम् ।
12.27.m: They should make the last [day] of the Abhiplava an Ukthya day; what belongs to the third pressing of the second day [serves as] the third pressing, the third pressing.

13.1.m: The Chandogas (Sāmaveda chanters) and the Adhvaryus are the first-performers.
If they should do what is not prescribed:

13.1.s: stotriye chandogam ahar yoge stoma vikāre pṛṣṭhe saṃsthāyām ca |
13.1.d: स्तोत्रिये छन्दोगम् अहर् योगे स्तोम विकारे पृष्ठे संस्थायाम् च ।
13.1.m: In respect to the stotriya verse, [the Hotṛ follows] the Chandoga in the connection of the day, in the modification of the stoma, in the pṛṣṭha, and in the concluding form of the sacrifice.

13.1.s: te cet pādam vā ardharcam vā viparyasyeyur ūnam vā atiriktam vā kuryur na tad ādriyeta |
13.1.d: ते चेत् पादम् वा अर्धर्चम् वा विपर्यस्येयुर् ऊनम् वा अतिरिक्तम् वा कुर्युर् न तद् आद्रियेत ।
13.1.m: If they should invert a quarter-verse or a half-verse, or make [it] deficient or redundant, he should not pay heed to that.
He should conform only to an inversion of whole verses.

13.1.s: nyūṅkhanīyaś cet pādo vikarṣeṇa pūryeta tasya saṃkhyāya dvitīyam nyūṅkhanīyam |
13.1.d: न्यूङ्खनीयश् चेत् पादो विकर्षेण पूर्येत तस्य संख्याय द्वितीयम् न्यूङ्खनीयम् ।
13.1.m: If a quarter-verse that is to receive the nyūṅkha should be filled out by protraction, the nyūṅkha is to be applied to the second [vowel] of it after counting.

13.1.s: ūrdhvam tu svarāt samāna chandomānāni vyañjanāni lupyeran |
13.1.d: ऊर्ध्वम् तु स्वरात् समान छन्दोमानानि व्यञ्जनानि लुप्येरन् ।
13.1.m: After the vowel, however, consonants of equal metrical measure would be omitted.

13.2.s: ānīte paśau mṛte anupākṛte anyam ālabheta ṛtvigbhyas tam kārayet |
13.2.d: आनीते पशौ मृते अनुपाकृते अन्यम् आलभेत ऋत्विग्भ्यस् तम् कारयेत् ।
13.2.m: When the victim has been brought up, if it dies before being dedicated, he should seize another; he should have the [dead] one disposed of by the priests.

13.2.s: upākṛte vepamāne | yasmād bhīṣā avepiṣṭhās tato no abhayam kuru | paśūn naḥ sarvān gopāya namo rudrāya mīḷhuṣe | svāhā iti juhoti |
13.2.d: उपाकृते वेपमाने । यस्माद् भीषा अवेपिष्ठास् ततो नो अभयम् कुरु । पशून् नः सर्वान् गोपाय नमो रुद्राय मीऌहुषे । स्वाहा इति जुहोति ।
13.2.m: When it has been dedicated, if it trembles, he offers [with the verse]: "From whatever fear you trembled, therefrom make us fearlessness. Guard all our cattle; homage to the bountiful Rudra; svāhā!"
With: "From whatever fear you lowed..." if it lows.
With: "From whatever fear you fled..." if it flees.
With: "From whatever fear you sat down..." if it sits down.
With: "From whatever fear you have been quieted..." if it dies.

13.2.s: naṣṭe mṛte palāyite vā anyam tad rūpam tad devatyam paśum ālabheta |
13.2.d: नष्टे मृते पलायिते वा अन्यम् तद् रूपम् तद् देवत्यम् पशुम् आलभेत ।
13.2.m: If it is lost, dead, or has run away, he should seize another beast of that form and of that deity.

13.2.s: mṛtasya vapām puroḷāśam avadānāni iti itarasya vaṣaṭ kāreṣu upajuhuyāt |
13.2.d: मृतस्य वपाम् पुरोऌआशम् अवदानानि इति इतरस्य वषट् कारेषु उपजुहुयात् ।
13.2.m: He should offer the omentum, sacrificial cake, and cut-off portions of the dead one as secondary offerings during the vaṣaṭ-calls of the other [victim].

13.3.s: pravṛtteṣu mṛte prayājeṣu tena eva saṃsthāpyam |
13.3.d: प्रवृत्तेषु मृते प्रयाजेषु तेन एव संस्थाप्यम् ।
13.3.m: If the fore-offerings have begun and it dies, [the sacrifice] must be completed with that very one.

13.3.s: avadāne naṣṭe duṣṭe vimathite vājyam pratinidadhyāt |
13.3.d: अवदाने नष्टे दुष्टे विमथिते वाज्यम् प्रतिनिदध्यात् ।
13.3.m: If a cut-off portion is lost, corrupted, or snatched away, he should substitute clarified butter.
If the heart is lost, he should seize another [victim].

13.3.s: yadi ca kāmayeta ārti vimathitāra ṛccheyur iti kuvid aṅga yavam anta yavamanta ity āgnīdhrīye juhuyāt |
13.3.d: यदि च कामयेत आर्ति विमथितार ऋच्छेयुर् इति कुविद् अङ्ग यवम् अन्त यवमन्त इत्य् आग्नीध्रीये जुहुयात् ।
13.3.m: And if he should desire, "May misfortune fall upon the snatchers," he should offer in the Āgnīdhra fire with: "Doubtless, O barley-possessor, containing barley..." [RV 10.131.2].

13.3.s: aṣṭā padyām vaśāyām anūbandhyāyām garbhasya tvaco vapā rūpam phalī karaṇānām phālī karaṇān garbham iti śāmitre śrapayitvā itarasya vaṣaṭ kāreṣu śāmitra eva juhuyāt |
13.3.d: अष्टा पद्याम् वशायाम् अनूबन्ध्यायाम् गर्भस्य त्वचो वपा रूपम् फली करणानाम् फाली करणान् गर्भम् इति शामित्रे श्रपयित्वा इतरस्य वषट् कारेषु शामित्र एव जुहुयात् ।
13.3.m: In the case of an eight-footed barren cow as the subsequently bound victim, having boiled the foetus's skin in the form of an omentum and the grain-chaff as the foetus's cut portions in the Śāmitra fire, he should offer them in the Śāmitra fire itself at the vaṣaṭ-calls of the other [offering].

13.4.s: yūpe virūḷhe anapavṛtte tvāṣṭram bahu rūpam ālabheta |
13.4.d: यूपे विरूऌहे अनपवृत्ते त्वाष्ट्रम् बहु रूपम् आलभेत ।
13.4.m: If the sacrificial post has sprouted and has not fallen down, he should seize a many-coloured victim for Tvaṣṭṛ.

13.4.s: piśaṅga rūpaḥ subharo vayodhās tan nas turīpam adha poṣayitnu devas tvaṣṭā savitā viśva rūpa iti puronuvākhyāḥ |
13.4.d: पिशङ्ग रूपः सुभरो वयोधास् तन् नस् तुरीपम् अध पोषयित्नु देवस् त्वष्टा सविता विश्व रूप इति पुरोनुवाख्याः ।
13.4.m: "Of tawny form, well-bearing, conferring vigor..." [RV 3.48.2], "That seminal fluid of ours, then, bringing nourishment..." [RV 3.48.4], and "The divine Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, omniform..." [RV 3.55.19] are the introductory verses.

13.4.s: pra sū mahe suśaraṇāya prathama bhājam deva tvaṣṭar yadd ha cārutvam ānaḷ iti yājyāḥ |
13.4.d: प्र सू महे सुशरणाय प्रथम भाजम् देव त्वष्टर् यद्द् ह चारुत्वम् आनऌ इति याज्याः ।
13.4.m: "Forth indeed to the great, the good refuge, the first sharer..." [RV 4.34.1] and "O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, since you have attained excellence..." [RV 2.31.4] are the consecratory verses.

13.5.s: jñāna viṣaye vidviṣāṇayoḥ sutyayor ahnoḥ samnipātanam saṃsava ity ācakṣate |
13.5.d: ज्ञान विषये विद्विषाणयोः सुत्ययोर् अह्नोः सम्निपातनम् संसव इत्य् आचक्षते ।
13.5.m: The simultaneous occurrence of soma-pressing days of two rivals within the range of knowledge they call a saṃsava (rival pressing).

13.5.s: pūrve prātar anuvākam upākṛtya pūrve saṃsthāpayeyuḥ |
13.5.d: पूर्वे प्रातर् अनुवाकम् उपाकृत्य पूर्वे संस्थापयेयुः ।
13.5.m: Beginning the morning recitation earlier, they should conclude earlier.

13.5.s: saṃveśāya upaveśāya gāyatryai chandase abhibhṛtyai svāhā iti prātaḥ savane |
13.5.d: संवेशाय उपवेशाय गायत्र्यै छन्दसे अभिभृत्यै स्वाहा इति प्रातः सवने ।
13.5.m: With: "For reclining, for sitting down, for the Gāyatrī metre, for overcoming, svāhā!" at the morning pressing.
With: "...for the Triṣṭubh metre..." at the midday pressing.
With: "...for the Jagatī metre..." at the third pressing.

13.5.s: adhvaryum mṛtam icchan prājāpatyābhis tisṛbhir adhvaryuḥ prātaḥ savane juhuyāt |
13.5.d: अध्वर्युम् मृतम् इच्छन् प्राजापत्याभिस् तिसृभिर् अध्वर्युः प्रातः सवने जुहुयात् ।
13.5.m: If wishing the Adhvaryu dead, the Adhvaryu should offer at the morning pressing with three verses addressed to Prajāpati.
[Wishing] the Hotṛ [dead], the Hotṛ [offers] at the midday pressing.
[Wishing] the Udgātṛ [dead], the Udgātṛ [offers] at the third pressing.
[Wishing] the Brahman [dead], the Brahman [offers] at every pressing.
[Wishing] the sacrificer [dead], the sacrificer [offers] at every pressing.
Wishing all dead, all [offer] at every pressing.
They should use the Bṛhat and Rathantara [chants].
And the Ābhīka, the Ābhīśava, the Abhinidhana, and the Abhīvarta [sāmans].
The Kayāśubhīya [hymn, RV 1.165, for] the Marutvatīya[-śastra].
The Sajanīya [hymn, RV 2.12, for] the Niṣkevalya[-śastra].
While the others are concluding, he should perform a higher concluding form of sacrifice.
When they are performing an Atirātra, [he should perform] a Dvirātra (two-night rite).
When they are performing a Dvirātra, [he should perform] a Trirātra (three-night rite).

13.5.s: tasyām vā saṃsthāyām bhūyasīr dakṣiṇā dadyāt |
13.5.d: तस्याम् वा संस्थायाम् भूयसीर् दक्षिणा दद्यात् ।
13.5.m: Or in that same concluding form, he should give more extensive sacrificial gifts.

13.5.s: sravantyo vā viharanti vāyur ākāśaś ca |
13.5.d: स्रवन्त्यो वा विहरन्ति वायुर् आकाशश् च ।
13.5.m: Or the flowing [streams] arrange it, [or] the wind and space.

13.6.s: krīte some apahṛte anatinayan kālan anyam āhṛtya abhiṣuṇuyāt |
13.6.d: क्रीते सोमे अपहृते अनतिनयन् कालन् अन्यम् आहृत्य अभिषुणुयात् ।
13.6.m: If the Soma is stolen after being purchased, without letting the proper times slip by, one should press another [Soma] having fetched it.

13.6.s: soma āhārāya soma vikrayiṇe vā kiṃcid dadyāt |
13.6.d: सोम आहाराय सोम विक्रयिणे वा किंचिद् दद्यात् ।
13.6.m: One should give something to the one who brought the Soma or to the Soma seller.

13.6.s: anadhigamyamāne pūtīkān śveta puṣpāṇy arjunāni kuśān vā bhiṣutya pratiduhā prātaḥ savane śrīṇīyāt śvetena mādhyandine dadhnā tṛtīya savane |
13.6.d: अनधिगम्यमाने पूतीकान् श्वेत पुष्पाण्य् अर्जुनानि कुशान् वा भिषुत्य प्रतिदुहा प्रातः सवने श्रीणीयात् श्वेतेन माध्यन्दिने दध्ना तृतीय सवने ।
13.6.m: If it is not to be found, having pressed pūtīka plants, or white-flowering arjuna plants, or kuśa grass, one should mix [it] with freshly milked warm milk at the morning pressing, with boiled milk at the midday [pressing], and with curds at the third pressing.

13.6.s: ekām gām dakṣiṇām dattvā avabhṛthād udetya punar dīkṣeta |
13.6.d: एकाम् गाम् दक्षिणाम् दत्त्वा अवभृथाद् उदेत्य पुनर् दीक्षेत ।
13.6.m: Having given one cow as the sacrificial fee, having come up from the purificatory bath, he should be consecrated again.
There he should give the sacrificial fees prescribed for the ritual.
If [the Soma] is burnt, he should give five cows as the sacrificial fee.

13.7.m: If Soma is left over from the morning pressing:

13.7.s: asti somo ayam suta iti stotriya anurūpau hotuḥ |
13.7.d: अस्ति सोमो अयम् सुत इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ होतुः ।
13.7.m: The stotriya and anurūpa verses for the Hotṛ are: 'asti somo ayaṃ sutaḥ' ('This soma is pressed').
He should over-recite the stoma with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.

13.7.s: indram id gāthino bṛhad ato devā avantu na iti ṣaṭ |
13.7.d: इन्द्रम् इद् गाथिनो बृहद् अतो देवा अवन्तु न इति षट् ।
13.7.m: The six verses beginning with 'indram id gāthino bṛhat' ('Indra indeed the singers [praise] with the Bṛhat') and 'ato devā avantu naḥ' ('From here let the gods help us').

13.7.s: uttamayā paridhāya viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyata iti yajati |
13.7.d: उत्तमया परिधाय विष्णोः कर्माणि पश्यत इति यजति ।
13.7.m: Having concluded with the last [verse], he recites the offering verse: 'viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyata' ('Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu').

13.8.m: If [Soma] is left over from the midday [pressing]:

13.8.s: baṇ mahān ud u tyad darśatam iti stotriya anurūpau pragāthau |
13.8.d: बण् महान् उद् उ त्यद् दर्शतम् इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ प्रगाथौ ।
13.8.m: The stotriya and anurūpa pragāthas are: 'baṇ mahān' ('Truly great') and 'ud u tyad darśatam' ('Up that visible [light]').
He should over-recite the stoma with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.

13.9.m: If [Soma] is left over from the third pressing:

13.9.s: pra tat te adya śipiviṣṭa pra tad viṣṇur iti stotriya anurūpau |
13.9.d: प्र तत् ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट प्र तद् विष्णुर् इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ ।
13.9.m: The stotriya and anurūpa verses are: 'pra tat te adya śipiviṣṭa' ('Forth that of thine today, O Śipiviṣṭa') and 'pra tad viṣṇuḥ' ('Forth that Viṣṇu').
He should over-recite the stoma with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.

13.10.m: He should over-recite the stoma with verses addressed to the Aśvins.

13.10.s: astutam cet paryāyair abhivyuccheta pañcabhiḥ stomair hotrakebhyaḥ stuvate |
13.10.d: अस्तुतम् चेत् पर्यायैर् अभिव्युच्छेत पञ्चभिः स्तोमैर् होत्रकेभ्यः स्तुवते ।
13.10.m: If the morning dawns before [the rounds of chants] are sung, they chant for the Hotrakas with five stomas.

13.10.s: te stotriya anurūpān śastvā uktha mukhānām jagatīnām ca dve dve śaṃseyuḥ |
13.10.d: ते स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपान् शस्त्वा उक्थ मुखानाम् जगतीनाम् च द्वे द्वे शंसेयुः ।
13.10.m: They, having recited the stotriya and anurūpa verses, should recite two verses each of the ukthamukhas and of the jagatī verses.
Or [they chant] with all the first rounds.
Or for the Hotṛ from the first rounds;
for the Maitrāvaruṇa and the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin from the middle rounds;
for the Acchāvāka from the final [rounds].
The Āśvina-śastra has three hundred and sixty [verses].

13.11.s: yadi dīkṣitaḥ pramīyeta dagdhvā asthīny upanahya putram bhrātaram vā dīkṣayitvā saha yajeran |
13.11.d: यदि दीक्षितः प्रमीयेत दग्ध्वा अस्थीन्य् उपनह्य पुत्रम् भ्रातरम् वा दीक्षयित्वा सह यजेरन् ।
13.11.m: If a consecrated sacrificer should die, having burned [him], tied up the bones, and consecrated his son or brother, they should sacrifice together.

13.11.s: abhiṣutya vā rājānam agṛhītvā grahān dakṣiṇā parasyām vedi śroṇyām asthi kumbham nidhāya tasmin deśe sārparājñībhiḥ parācībhiḥ stuvate |
13.11.d: अभिषुत्य वा राजानम् अगृहीत्वा ग्रहान् दक्षिणा परस्याम् वेदि श्रोण्याम् अस्थि कुम्भम् निधाय तस्मिन् देशे सार्पराज्ञीभिः पराचीभिः स्तुवते ।
13.11.m: Or, having pressed King [Soma] without drawing the cups, having deposited the urn of bones on the southern rear hip of the sacrificial altar, they chant in that place with the Sārparājñī verses without repetition.

13.11.s: triḥ prasavyam mārjālīyam pariyanti savyān ūrūn apāghnātāḥ |
13.11.d: त्रिः प्रसव्यम् मार्जालीयम् परियन्ति सव्यान् ऊरून् अपाघ्नाताः ।
13.11.m: Beating their left thighs, they walk three times counter-clockwise around the Mārjālīya.
The Hotṛ should recite the Sārparājñī verses.
The cups are those that begin with the cup for Indra and Vāyu.
After a year they should perform the sacrifice with the bones.
At every chant they set down the urn of bones close by.
They pour out the portions [of Soma] at the Mārjālīya.

13.12.s: kalaśe dīrṇe vidhum dadrāṇam iti vaṣaṭ kāra nidhanena brāhmaṇācchaṃsine stuvate |
13.12.d: कलशे दीर्णे विधुम् दद्राणम् इति वषट् कार निधनेन ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिने स्तुवते ।
13.12.m: If the kalaśa jar is broken, they chant for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [a chant] ending with a vaṣaṭ-call: 'vidhuṃ dadrāṇam' ('The wandering moon').

13.12.s: grāvṇi dīrṇe vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇā iti dyutānena mārutena brāhmaṇācchaṃsine stuvate |
13.12.d: ग्राव्णि दीर्णे वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथाद् ईषमाणा इति द्युतानेन मारुतेन ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिने स्तुवते ।
13.12.m: If the pressing-stone is broken, they chant for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin the Dyutāna chant addressed to the Maruts: 'vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇāḥ' ('Fleeing from the snorting of Vṛtra').
He should over-recite the stoma with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.

13.12.s: abhyunnītam nārāśaṃsam | huta ahutasya tṛmpatam hutasya ca ahutasya ca | ahutasya hutasya ca indra agnī asya somasya | svāhā ity antaḥ paridhi bhasmani juhoti |
13.12.d: अभ्युन्नीतम् नाराशंसम् । हुत अहुतस्य तृम्पतम् हुतस्य च अहुतस्य च । अहुतस्य हुतस्य च इन्द्र अग्नी अस्य सोमस्य । स्वाहा इत्य् अन्तः परिधि भस्मनि जुहोति ।
13.12.m: Upon the Nārāśaṃsa cup that has been replenished, he makes an offering into the ashes within the enclosing sticks, saying: 'Of what is offered and what is unoffered, be satisfied; both of what is offered and what is unoffered; of what is unoffered and what is offered, O Indra and Agni, of this Soma, svāhā!'

13.12.s: upavāte nārāśaṃse yam jaghanyam graham gṛhṇīyāt tasya hutasya alpakam avanayet prajāpataye svāhā iti |
13.12.d: उपवाते नाराशंसे यम् जघन्यम् ग्रहम् गृह्णीयात् तस्य हुतस्य अल्पकम् अवनयेत् प्रजापतये स्वाहा इति ।
13.12.m: If the Nārāśaṃsa cup is contaminated by wind, he should pour down a small portion of the last cup he draws, after it has been offered, saying: 'To Prajāpati, svāhā!'

13.12.s: duṣṭam somam prājāpatyābhiś catasṛbhir adhvaryur uttara ardha pūrva ardha uparave avanayet |
13.12.d: दुष्टम् सोमम् प्राजापत्याभिश् चतसृभिर् अध्वर्युर् उत्तर अर्ध पूर्व अर्ध उपरवे अवनयेत् ।
13.12.m: The Adhvaryu should pour down spoiled Soma into the northern, eastern, and western sounding-holes with four verses addressed to Prajāpati.

13.12.s: kṛtsnam vedam amṛtam anna adya bhāgam iti dhyāyann avavṛṣṭasya bhakṣayed indur indram avāgāt tasya tu indrav indra pītasya upahūtasya upahūto bhakṣayāmi iti |
13.12.d: कृत्स्नम् वेदम् अमृतम् अन्न अद्य भागम् इति ध्यायन्न् अववृष्टस्य भक्षयेद् इन्दुर् इन्द्रम् अवागात् तस्य तु इन्द्रव् इन्द्र पीतस्य उपहूतस्य उपहूतो भक्षयामि इति ।
13.12.m: Meditating, 'The whole Veda, immortality, the share of food and drink,' he should consume [Soma] upon which rain has fallen, saying: 'The drop has gone down into Indra; of it, O Indra, drunk by Indra, invited, invited I consume.'

13.12.s: hiraṇya garbha ity abhyupākṛte camase juhuyāt |
13.12.d: हिरण्य गर्भ इत्य् अभ्युपाकृते चमसे जुहुयात् ।
13.12.m: He should make an offering into the cup brought forward, with: 'hiraṇyagarbhaḥ' ('The Golden Germ').

13.12.s: ya ṛte cid iti tṛcena mahā vīram bhinnam anumantrya | trayas triṃśat tantavo ye vitnire ya imam yajñam svadhayā bhajante | teṣām chinnam sam imam dadhāmi svāhā gharmo apyetu devān | yajñasya doho vitataḥ purutrā so aṣṭadhā divam anvātatāna | sa yajña dhukṣva mahi me prajāyai rāyas poṣam viśvamāyur aśīya | svāhā iti ca āhutī juhoti |
13.12.d: य ऋते चिद् इति तृचेन महा वीरम् भिन्नम् अनुमन्त्र्य । त्रयस् त्रिंशत् तन्तवो ये वित्निरे य इमम् यज्ञम् स्वधया भजन्ते । तेषाम् छिन्नम् सम् इमम् दधामि स्वाहा घर्मो अप्येतु देवान् । यज्ञस्य दोहो विततः पुरुत्रा सो अष्टधा दिवम् अन्वाततान । स यज्ञ धुक्ष्व महि मे प्रजायै रायस् पोषम् विश्वमायुर् अशीय । स्वाहा इति च आहुती जुहोति ।
13.12.m:
And having covered it, he should carry it out.
Having addressed the broken Mahāvīra pot with the triplet 'ya ṛte cid' ('Even without...'), [he offers with:] 'Thirty-three threads which are stretched out, which share in this sacrifice according to svadhā; what of theirs is severed, this I join together, svāhā! May the Gharma go unto the gods!'
And he offers [a second] oblation with: 'The milch-yield of the sacrifice is stretched out manifold; that has expanded eightfold unto the sky. Do thou, O sacrifice, milk great abundance of wealth for my offspring; may I attain a full lifetime, svāhā!'

13.13.s: yadi satrāya dīkṣito atha sāmyuttiṣṭhet somam apabhajya rājānam viśvajitā atirātreṇa yajeta sarva stomena sarva pṛṣṭhena sarva vedasa dakṣiṇena |
13.13.d: यदि सत्राय दीक्षितो अथ साम्युत्तिष्ठेत् सोमम् अपभज्य राजानम् विश्वजिता अतिरात्रेण यजेत सर्व स्तोमेन सर्व पृष्ठेन सर्व वेदस दक्षिणेन ।
13.13.m: If one has been consecrated for a sacrificial session (sattra) and then leaves in the middle, having apportioned King Soma, he should sacrifice with a Viśvajit Atirātra, having all the stomas, all the pṛṣṭhas, and with his entire property as the sacrificial fee.

13.14.s: āhita agnaya iṣṭa prathama yajñā dīkṣitā gṛhapati saptadaśāḥ satram āsīran hotā maitrāvaruṇo acchāvāko grāvastud brahmā brāhmaṇācchaṃsī potā āgnīdhra udgātā prastotā pratihartā subrahmaṇyo adhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātā neṣṭā unnetā |
13.14.d: आहित अग्नय इष्ट प्रथम यज्ञा दीक्षिता गृहपति सप्तदशाः सत्रम् आसीरन् होता मैत्रावरुणो अच्छावाको ग्रावस्तुद् ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी पोता आग्नीध्र उद्गाता प्रस्तोता प्रतिहर्ता सुब्रह्मण्यो अध्वर्युः प्रतिप्रस्थाता नेष्टा उन्नेता ।
13.14.m: Those who have established their sacred fires, who have performed their first sacrifice, and are consecrated, seventeen in number including the master of the house, should sit for a sacrificial session: Hotṛ, Maitrāvaruṇa, Acchāvāka, Grāvastut, Brahman, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Potṛ, Āgnīdhra, Udgātṛ, Prastotṛ, Pratihārtṛ, Subrahmaṇya, Adhvaryu, Pratiprasthātṛ, Neṣṭṛ, and Unnetṛ.
When simultaneity is impossible without conflict with the priestly duties,
the duties of the sacrificer belong to all [of them] in the order of consecration.
The leader should perform the acts done on behalf of others.
In case of conflict of ritual rules, the common practice belongs to the majority.

13.14.s: huteṣu dākṣiṇeṣu dakṣiṇā pathena kṛṣṇa ajināni dhunvanto ahar ahar ity āvrajeyur idam aham mām kalyāṇyai kīrtyai svargāya lokāya amṛtatvāya dakṣiṇām nayāni iti |
13.14.d: हुतेषु दाक्षिणेषु दक्षिणा पथेन कृष्ण अजिनानि धुन्वन्तो अहर् अहर् इत्य् आव्रजेयुर् इदम् अहम् माम् कल्याण्यै कीर्त्यै स्वर्गाय लोकाय अमृतत्वाय दक्षिणाम् नयानि इति ।
13.14.m: When the offerings for the sacrificial gifts have been poured, they should proceed along the path of the sacrificial gifts, shaking black antelope skins [and saying]: 'Day by day, here I lead the sacrificial gift for good fame, for the heavenly world, for immortality.'

13.14.s: ukthāya ca agniṣṭomaḥ sahasra dakṣiṇaḥ pṛṣṭha śamanīyaḥ |
13.14.d: उक्थाय च अग्निष्टोमः सहस्र दक्षिणः पृष्ठ शमनीयः ।
13.14.m: And for the Ukthya, [there is] an Agniṣṭoma with a thousand [cows as] sacrificial gift, [serving as] the appeaser of the Pṛṣṭha rites.
Some indeed [hold that] the appeaser of the Pṛṣṭha rites is common [to both].

13.14.s: dvādaśa aha prabhṛtīnyā catvāriṃśad rātrād eka uttarāṇi rātri satrāṇi teṣu nityaḥ |
13.14.d: द्वादश अह प्रभृतीन्या चत्वारिंशद् रात्राद् एक उत्तराणि रात्रि सत्राणि तेषु नित्यः ।
13.14.m: The night-sessions beginning with twelve days up to forty nights increase by one [day each]; in these it is regular.

13.14.s: dvādaśa aho yair ahobhir vivardhate tāny udāhariṣyāmaḥ |
13.14.d: द्वादश अहो यैर् अहोभिर् विवर्धते तान्य् उदाहरिष्यामः ।
13.14.m: We shall set forth the days by which the twelve-day rite increases.

13.15.s: eka aha arthe mahā vratam āharanti |
13.15.d: एक अह अर्थे महा व्रतम् आहरन्ति ।
13.15.m: For the sake of a single day, they introduce the Mahāvrata;
Or an Atirātra containing all the stomas,
Between the Pṛṣṭhya [six-day period] and the Chandomas.

13.15.s: dvitīyam tṛtīyam ca abhiplavike pratīyeta etasyām codanāyām |
13.15.d: द्वितीयम् तृतीयम् च अभिप्लविके प्रतीयेत एतस्याम् चोदनायाम् ।
13.15.m: In this prescription, the second and third [days] of the Abhiplava should be understood.

13.15.s: try aha arthe trīṇi pūrvāṇy ābhiplavikāni |
13.15.d: त्र्य् अह अर्थे त्रीणि पूर्वाण्य् आभिप्लविकानि ।
13.15.m: For the sake of a three-day rite, [they introduce] the first three [days] of the Abhiplava.

13.15.s: catur aha arthe mahā vrata caturthāni |
13.15.d: चतुर् अह अर्थे महा व्रत चतुर्थानि ।
13.15.m: For the sake of a four-day rite, [they introduce three days] ending with the Mahāvrata as the fourth.

13.15.s: sapta aha arthe mahā vrata saptamāni |
13.15.d: सप्त अह अर्थे महा व्रत सप्तमानि ।
13.15.m: For the sake of a seven-day rite, [they introduce six days] ending with the Mahāvrata as the seventh.

13.15.s: etena nyāyena tām tām saṃkhyām pūrayanti |
13.15.d: एतेन न्यायेन ताम् ताम् संख्याम् पूरयन्ति ।
13.15.m: By this rule they fill up each respective number.

13.15.s: antareṇa prāyaṇīyam pṛṣṭhyam ca eteṣām sthānam |
13.15.d: अन्तरेण प्रायणीयम् पृष्ठ्यम् च एतेषाम् स्थानम् ।
13.15.m: Their place is between the introductory rite and the Pṛṣṭhya [six-day period].

13.15.s: ūrdhvam tu daśamād ahno mahā vratasya sthānam |
13.15.d: ऊर्ध्वम् तु दशमाद् अह्नो महा व्रतस्य स्थानम् ।
13.15.m: The place of the Mahāvrata, however, is after the tenth day.

13.16.s: abhiplavo abhijid viśvajitau ca āgantūni viṃśati rātre |
13.16.d: अभिप्लवो अभिजिद् विश्वजितौ च आगन्तूनि विंशति रात्रे ।
13.16.m: In a twenty-night session, the Abhiplava and the Abhijit and Viśvajit are inserted.

13.16.s: abhiplavo atirātro dvāv abhiplavāv ity eka viṃśati rātraḥ pūrvaḥ |
13.16.d: अभिप्लवो अतिरात्रो द्वाव् अभिप्लवाव् इत्य् एक विंशति रात्रः पूर्वः ।
13.16.m: An Abhiplava, an Atirātra, and two Abhiplavas: this is the former twenty-one-night rite.

13.16.s: pṛṣṭhyaḥ svara sāmāno viṣuvān āvṛttāḥ svara sāmānas trayas triṃśa ārambhaṇaḥ pṛṣṭhya ity uttaraḥ |
13.16.d: पृष्ठ्यः स्वर सामानो विषुवान् आवृत्ताः स्वर सामानस् त्रयस् त्रिंश आरम्भणः पृष्ठ्य इत्य् उत्तरः ।
13.16.m: A Pṛṣṭhya, the Svarasāman days, the Viṣuvant day, the reversed Svarasāman days, and a Pṛṣṭhya beginning with the thirty-three-fold stoma: this is the latter [twenty-one-night rite].

13.16.s: pṛṣṭhya sotmaḥ ṣaḷ ahaḥ | trayas triṃśam ahar aniruktam | trayas triṃśa ārambhaṇaḥ pṛṣṭhya stomaḥ ṣaḷ ahaḥ | trivṛd ahar aniruktam | jyotiṣṭomo agniṣṭoma iti catur viṃśati rātraḥ saṃsadām ayanam ity ācakṣate |
13.16.d: पृष्ठ्य सोत्मः षऌ अहः । त्रयस् त्रिंशम् अहर् अनिरुक्तम् । त्रयस् त्रिंश आरम्भणः पृष्ठ्य स्तोमः षऌ अहः । त्रिवृद् अहर् अनिरुक्तम् । ज्योतिष्टोमो अग्निष्टोम इति चतुर् विंशति रात्रः संसदाम् अयनम् इत्य् आचक्षते ।
13.16.m: A Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, an unexpressed thirty-three-fold day, a Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite beginning with the thirty-three-fold stoma, an unexpressed nine-fold day, and a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma: this is the twenty-four-night rite; they call it the course of the assemblies.

13.17.s: pañca ābhiplavikāni trir upetya viśvajid atirātra eṣa eva pañca aho daśa rātra iti trayas triṃśad rātraḥ |
13.17.d: पञ्च आभिप्लविकानि त्रिर् उपेत्य विश्वजिद् अतिरात्र एष एव पञ्च अहो दश रात्र इति त्रयस् त्रिंशद् रात्रः ।
13.17.m: Having undertaken five Abhiplava days three times, [then] a Viśvajit Atirātra, and just this five-day period [and] the ten-day period: this is the thirty-three-night rite.

13.17.s: caturviṃśam abhiplavaḥ pṛṣṭhyo nava aho go āyuṣī daśa rātro mahā vratam iti sapta triṃśad rātraḥ |
13.17.d: चतुर्विंशम् अभिप्लवः पृष्ठ्यो नव अहो गो आयुषी दश रात्रो महा व्रतम् इति सप्त त्रिंशद् रात्रः ।

13.17.s: catur viṃśam trayo abhiplavāḥ | abhijit svara sāmāno viṣuvān āvṛttāḥ svara sāmāno viśvajic ca | abhijit prabhṛti nava rātra ity ācakṣate | abhiplavo go āyuṣī daśa rātro mahā vratam | ity enānna pañcāśad rātraḥ | saṃvatsara sammitaḥ |
13.17.d: चतुर् विंशम् त्रयो अभिप्लवाः । अभिजित् स्वर सामानो विषुवान् आवृत्ताः स्वर सामानो विश्वजिच् च । अभिजित् प्रभृति नव रात्र इत्य् आचक्षते । अभिप्लवो गो आयुषी दश रात्रो महा व्रतम् । इत्य् एनान्न पञ्चाशद् रात्रः । संवत्सर सम्मितः ।
13.17.m:
The twenty-fourth [day], an Abhiplava, a Pṛṣṭhya, a nine-day period, the Go and Āyus days, the ten-day period, and the Mahāvrata: this is the thirty-seven-night rite. / The twenty-fourth [day], three Abhiplavas, the Abhijit, the Svarasāman days, the Viṣuvant day, the reversed Svarasāman days, and the Viśvajit; they call [the days] beginning with the Abhijit the nine-night rite.
An Abhiplava, the Go and Āyus days, the ten-day period, and the Mahāvrata: this is the forty-nine-night rite, commensurate with the year.

13.18.m: On both sides of the nine-night period there are two six-day rites.
The hundred-night rite is arranged according to the standard rule.

13.18.s: ardha pañcadaśa abhiplavās teṣām prathamas tryaho daśarātro mahā vratam iti |
13.18.d: अर्ध पञ्चदश अभिप्लवास् तेषाम् प्रथमस् त्र्यहो दशरात्रो महा व्रतम् इति ।
13.18.m: Fourteen and a half Abhiplavas, of which the first is a three-day rite, then the ten-day rite, [and] the Mahāvrata.

13.19.m: The consecration of the Gavāmayana lasts seventeen [days];

13.19.s: taiṣasya amāvāsyāyā ekāha upariṣṭād dīkṣeran māghasya vā |
13.19.d: तैषस्य अमावास्याया एकाह उपरिष्टाद् दीक्षेरन् माघस्य वा ।
13.19.m: They should consecrate themselves one day after the New Moon of the month Taiṣa, or of Māgha.

13.19.s: teṣām māghasya amāvāsyāyām upavasathaḥ phālgunasya vā |
13.19.d: तेषाम् माघस्य अमावास्यायाम् उपवसथः फाल्गुनस्य वा ।
13.19.m: For them, the day of preparation is on the New Moon of Māgha, or of Phālguna.

13.19.s: dvādaśa dīkṣāḥ kurvāṇāś catur ahe purastāt paurṇamāsyā dīkṣeran |
13.19.d: द्वादश दीक्षाः कुर्वाणाश् चतुर् अहे पुरस्तात् पौर्णमास्या दीक्षेरन् ।
13.19.m: Those observing twelve consecration days should consecrate themselves four days before the Full Moon.
For them, the soma-pressing begins on the fifth day of the bright fortnight.

13.19.s: prāyaṇīyam atirātram upetya caturviṃśam ca pṛṣṭhya pañcamāṃś caturo abhiplavān upayanti |
13.19.d: प्रायणीयम् अतिरात्रम् उपेत्य चतुर्विंशम् च पृष्ठ्य पञ्चमांश् चतुरो अभिप्लवान् उपयन्ति ।
13.19.m: Having undertaken the introductory Atirātra and the twenty-fourth [day], they undertake four Abhiplavas with a Pṛṣṭhya as the fifth.

13.19.s: tathā yuktān pañca māsān upetya pṛṣṭhya caturthān abhiplavān upayanti |
13.19.d: तथा युक्तान् पञ्च मासान् उपेत्य पृष्ठ्य चतुर्थान् अभिप्लवान् उपयन्ति ।
13.19.m: Having undertaken five months composed in this manner, they undertake Abhiplavas with a Pṛṣṭhya as the fourth;

13.19.s: ūrdhvam viśvajitaḥ pṛṣṭhya ārambhaṇān māsān upayanti |
13.19.d: ऊर्ध्वम् विश्वजितः पृष्ठ्य आरम्भणान् मासान् उपयन्ति ।
13.19.m: After the Viśvajit, they undertake months beginning with a Pṛṣṭhya.
And the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava should be reversed day by day;
And the Vaiśvadeva hymns of the last Abhiplava days [are reversed].
Having undertaken a Pṛṣṭhya, [they undertake] three Abhiplavas.

13.19.s: pṛṣṭhyam upetya caturo abhiplavān | tathā yuktāṃś caturo māsān upetya trīn abhiplavān upayanty āyur gām daśarātram mahā vratam atirātram ca |
13.19.d: पृष्ठ्यम् उपेत्य चतुरो अभिप्लवान् । तथा युक्तांश् चतुरो मासान् उपेत्य त्रीन् अभिप्लवान् उपयन्त्य् आयुर् गाम् दशरात्रम् महा व्रतम् अतिरात्रम् च ।
13.19.m: Having undertaken a Pṛṣṭhya, [then] four Abhiplavas, and having undertaken four months composed in this manner, they undertake three Abhiplavas, the Āyus and Go days, the ten-day period, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra.
Such is the arrangement of the days of the Gavāmayana.
The year-long sacrificial sessions have that as their model.
In them, modification occurs elsewhere than in the ten-day period.

13.19.s: pṛṣṭhyasya abhiplavaḥ sthāne tad abhiplava ayanam |
13.19.d: पृष्ठ्यस्य अभिप्लवः स्थाने तद् अभिप्लव अयनम् ।
13.19.m: An Abhiplava [takes place] in the position of the Pṛṣṭhya; that is the Abhiplava-course.

13.20.s: yāni paurṇamāsībhiḥ sutyāny ahāni samnipateyus tāny utsṛjeran |
13.20.d: यानि पौर्णमासीभिः सुत्यान्य् अहानि सम्निपतेयुस् तान्य् उत्सृजेरन् ।
13.20.m: Whichever pressing days coincide with the Full Moon days, those they should omit;
Or [those coinciding with] both the New and Full Moon days.
Or they should perform the single-and-triple stoma;
Or they should omit one verse of the chanting verses [each day],
When skipping a day, they should sacrifice on that day with an animal [victim] dedicated to Prajāpati;

13.20.s: ahar utsṛjamānāḥ prājāpatyena tad ahaḥ paśunā yajeran |
13.20.d: अहर् उत्सृजमानाः प्राजापत्येन तद् अहः पशुना यजेरन् ।

13.20.m: or [with one] dedicated to whichever deity the savanīya [animal victim] belongs to.
There, within the framework of the animal sacrifice, they bring the sacrificial offerings into line.

13.20.s: teṣām sa dharmo yaḥ paśu tantre codyamānānām |
13.20.d: तेषाम् स धर्मो यः पशु तन्त्रे चोद्यमानानाम् ।
13.20.m: The rule for them is that which applies to those prescribed in the framework of the animal sacrifice.
They should make the stotriyā verses of the following day into corresponding [anurūpa] verses,
as appropriate, with the extraordinary ritual summonses.
And having concluded, they should sit for twelve days.
Omitting both [types of days, there is] the Course of the Sessions.

13.21.s: trivṛt pañcadaśāv abhiplava stomau pūrvasmin paṭale |
13.21.d: त्रिवृत् पञ्चदशाव् अभिप्लव स्तोमौ पूर्वस्मिन् पटले ।
13.21.m: The Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa are the two Abhiplava stomas in the first half [of the year];
the Pañcadaśa and Trivṛt in the second.
In the middle are the Pṛṣṭhya months.

13.21.s: ṣaṣṭhe māsi trīn abhiplavān upetya pṛṣṭhyam upayanti nava rātram ca |
13.21.d: षष्ठे मासि त्रीन् अभिप्लवान् उपेत्य पृष्ठ्यम् उपयन्ति नव रात्रम् च ।
13.21.m: In the sixth month, having undertaken three Abhiplavas, they undertake a Pṛṣṭhya and a nine-day rite.
In place of the Abhijit [there is] the Bṛhaspatisava;
the Indrastoma in place of the Viśvajit.

13.21.s: pṛṣṭhyam upetya abhiplavam ca vyūḷha chandasam daśarātram |
13.21.d: पृष्ठ्यम् उपेत्य अभिप्लवम् च व्यूऌह छन्दसम् दशरात्रम् ।
13.21.m: Having undertaken a Pṛṣṭhya and an Abhiplava, [there is] the ten-day rite with transposed metres;
the stoma in the Trivṛt is in the form of an Agniṣṭoma;

13.21.s: madhye pṛṣṭhyāṃś caturo māsān upetya madhye pṛṣṭhyāv abhiplavā upayanti |
13.21.d: मध्ये पृष्ठ्यांश् चतुरो मासान् उपेत्य मध्ये पृष्ठ्याव् अभिप्लवा उपयन्ति ।
13.21.m: Having undertaken the four months with Pṛṣṭhyas in the middle, they undertake two Abhiplavas with Pṛṣṭhyas in the middle,

13.22.m: The Abhiplava stoma is the Trivṛt.

13.22.s: pṛṣṭhya ārambhaṇān māsān upayanti pūrvasmin paṭale |
13.22.d: पृष्ठ्य आरम्भणान् मासान् उपयन्ति पूर्वस्मिन् पटले ।
13.22.m: In the first half they undertake months beginning with a Pṛṣṭhya;
in the second half, ending with a Pṛṣṭhya.
The rest is identical to the Course of the Ādityas.

13.23.m: A month with each one of the Pṛṣṭhya stomas;

13.23.s: āvṛttānām pṛṣṭhya stomānām eka ekena māsam |
13.23.d: आवृत्तानाम् पृष्ठ्य स्तोमानाम् एक एकेन मासम् ।
13.23.m: a month with each one of the reversed Pṛṣṭhya stomas;
In the Serpent Session, the central day is a twelve-day period.

13.24.m: The Course of the Kauṇḍapāyins has consecrations for a month.

13.24.s: krītvā rājānam upanahya upasada upetya agnihotreṇa māsam |
13.24.d: क्रीत्वा राजानम् उपनह्य उपसद उपेत्य अग्निहोत्रेण मासम् ।
13.24.m: Having bought King [Soma], wrapped [it], and undertaken the Upasad days, [they perform] the Agnihotra for a month;
the New and Full Moon sacrifices for a month;
each single seasonal period [parvan] of the Cāturmāsyas for a month;

13.24.s: trivṛt prabhṛtīnām pañcānām pṛṣṭhya stomānām eka ekena māsam |
13.24.d: त्रिवृत् प्रभृतीनाम् पञ्चानाम् पृष्ठ्य स्तोमानाम् एक एकेन मासम् ।
13.24.m: each single one of the five Pṛṣṭhya stomas beginning with the Trivṛt for a month;

13.24.s: aṣṭādaśa aham trayas triṃśena daśa rātram mahā vratam atirātram ca iti |
13.24.d: अष्टादश अहम् त्रयस् त्रिंशेन दश रात्रम् महा व्रतम् अतिरात्रम् च इति ।
13.24.m: an eighteen-day period with the Trayastriṃśa [stoma], the ten-day period, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra.

13.24.s: yo hotā so adhvaryuḥ sa potā |
13.24.d: यो होता सो अध्वर्युः स पोता ।
13.24.m: He who is the Hotṛ is the Adhvaryu and the Potṛ.

13.24.s: yo maitrāvaruṇaḥ sa brahmā sa pratihartā |
13.24.d: यो मैत्रावरुणः स ब्रह्मा स प्रतिहर्ता ।
13.24.m: He who is the Maitrāvaruṇa is the Brahman and the Pratihartṛ.

13.24.s: ya udgātā so acchāvākaḥ sa neṣṭā |
13.24.d: य उद्गाता सो अच्छावाकः स नेष्टा ।
13.24.m: He who is the Udgātṛ is the Acchāvāka and the Neṣṭṛ.

13.24.s: yaḥ prastotā sa brāhmaṇācchaṃsī sa grāvastut |
13.24.d: यः प्रस्तोता स ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी स ग्रावस्तुत् ।
13.24.m: He who is the Prastotṛ is the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the Grāvastut.

13.24.s: ya pratiprasthātā yo agnīt sa unnetā |
13.24.d: य प्रतिप्रस्थाता यो अग्नीत् स उन्नेता ।
13.24.m: He who is the Pratiprasthātṛ and he who is the Āgnīdhra is the Unnetṛ.

13.24.s: deśa kāla samnikarṣe avaideśyā pradhānasya vaśam nayet |
13.24.d: देश काल सम्निकर्षे अवैदेश्या प्रधानस्य वशम् नयेत् ।
13.24.m: In the concurrence of place and time, what is not bound to a particular place should be subordinated to the primary rite.
When single-day rites are formed out of a composite ritual, they should cease [from modifying each other].

13.24.s: ayam yajñīya atipraiṣaḥ sapuronuvākyaḥ śvaḥ stotriyā hotrakāṇām kadvanta uktha mukhīyāś ca abhitaṣṭīyam iti tāyamāna rūpāṇi |
13.24.d: अयम् यज्ञीय अतिप्रैषः सपुरोनुवाक्यः श्वः स्तोत्रिया होत्रकाणाम् कद्वन्त उक्थ मुखीयाश् च अभितष्टीयम् इति तायमान रूपाणि ।
13.24.m: This [formula] 'O sacrificial one...', the extraordinary ritual summons accompanied by an introductory verse, the morrow's stotriyā verses of the Hotrakas, those beginning with 'kad', the ukthamukha verses, and the Abhitaṣṭīya chant are the forms performed in extension.
The arrangement of days is just like that of the Course of the Cows [Gavāmayana].

13.25.m: [There are] the first and last months of the Course of the Cows,
and two twenty-eight-day periods, and the central day.
That, they call the Minor Tāpaścita.

13.26.m: That they call the Tāpaścita rite.

13.27.m: In a sacrifice of many years, there is repetition of the Gavāmayana,
or leaving out the movable days.

13.27.s: atirātraḥ sahasram ahāny atirātro agneḥ sahasra sāvyam |
13.27.d: अतिरात्रः सहस्रम् अहान्य् अतिरात्रो अग्नेः सहस्र साव्यम् ।
13.27.m: An Atirātra, a thousand days, and an Atirātra constitute Agni's thousand-pressing sacrifice (Sahasrasāvya).

13.28.m: The Gavāmayana is the first year;
this is the three-year sacrifice for those desiring offspring.

13.28.s: trivṛt prabhṛtīnām caturṇām pṛṣṭhya stomānām eka ekena trīṃs trīn saṃvatsarān prajāpate dvādaśa saṃvatsaram |
13.28.d: त्रिवृत् प्रभृतीनाम् चतुर्णाम् पृष्ठ्य स्तोमानाम् एक एकेन त्रींस् त्रीन् संवत्सरान् प्रजापते द्वादश संवत्सरम् ।
13.28.m: With each single one of the four Pṛṣṭhya-stomas, beginning with the Trivṛt, [performed] for three years each, is Prajāpati's twelve-year sacrifice.

13.28.s: eteṣām eva eka ekena nava nava śaktyānām ṣaṭ triṃśat saṃvatsaram |
13.28.d: एतेषाम् एव एक एकेन नव नव शक्त्यानाम् षट् त्रिंशत् संवत्सरम् ।
13.28.m: With each single one of these [stomas performed] for nine [years] each is the thirty-six-year sacrifice of the Śāktyas.

13.28.s: eteṣām eva eka ekena pañca viṃśatiḥ pañca viṃśatiḥ sādhyānām śata saṃvatsaram |
13.28.d: एतेषाम् एव एक एकेन पञ्च विंशतिः पञ्च विंशतिः साध्यानाम् शत संवत्सरम् ।
13.28.m: With each single one of these [stomas performed] for twenty-five [years] each is the hundred-year sacrifice of the Sādhyas.

13.28.s: eteṣām eva eka ekena pañca pañca pañcāśato viśvasṛjām sahasra saṃvatsaram |
13.28.d: एतेषाम् एव एक एकेन पञ्च पञ्च पञ्चाशतो विश्वसृजाम् सहस्र संवत्सरम् ।
13.28.m: With each single one of these [stomas performed] for two hundred and fifty [years] each is the thousand-year sacrifice of the Viśvasṛjs.

13.29.s: krītvā rājānam upanahya upasada upetya | prāyaṇīyam atirātram upetya | iṣṭvā sāmnāyyena adhvaryuḥ śamyām parāsya | tatra gārhapatyam nidhāya ṣaṭ ktriṃśat prakrameṣv āhavanīyam abhyādadhāti |
13.29.d: क्रीत्वा राजानम् उपनह्य उपसद उपेत्य । प्रायणीयम् अतिरात्रम् उपेत्य । इष्ट्वा साम्नाय्येन अध्वर्युः शम्याम् परास्य । तत्र गार्हपत्यम् निधाय षट् क्त्रिंशत् प्रक्रमेष्व् आहवनीयम् अभ्यादधाति ।
13.29.m:
The consecration of the Sarasvatī session takes place at the disappearance of the Sarasvatī. Having purchased the King [Soma], tied him up, undergone the Upasads, and undergone the introductory Atirātra; having offered the curd and milk offering, the Adhvaryu hurls a yoke-pin;
having placed the Gārhapatya there, he sets up the Āhavanīya at [a distance of] thirty-six steps.

13.29.s: tam etam āpūryamāṇa pakṣam āmāvāsyena yanti |
13.29.d: तम् एतम् आपूर्यमाण पक्षम् आमावास्येन यन्ति ।
13.29.m: They go through this waxing fortnight with the New Moon rite.

13.29.s: teṣām paurṇamāsyām gaur ukthyo bṛhat sāmā |
13.29.d: तेषाम् पौर्णमास्याम् गौर् उक्थ्यो बृहत् सामा ।
13.29.m: On their Full Moon day, there is a Gauḥ Ukthya day with the Bṛhat chant.

13.29.s: tam etam apakṣīyamāṇa pakṣam paurṇamāsyena yanti |
13.29.d: तम् एतम् अपक्षीयमाण पक्षम् पौर्णमास्येन यन्ति ।
13.29.m: They go through this waning fortnight with the Full Moon rite.

13.29.s: teṣām amāvāsyāyām āyur ukthyo rathantara sāmā |
13.29.d: तेषाम् अमावास्यायाम् आयुर् उक्थ्यो रथन्तर सामा ।
13.29.m: On their New Moon day, there is an Āyus Ukthya day with the Rathantara chant.
They proceed upstream with the former wing.
Having offered a boiled rice-mess to Apāṃ Napāt;

13.29.s: tad asya anīkam asmin pada ity aponaputriyasya |
13.29.d: तद् अस्य अनीकम् अस्मिन् पद इत्य् अपोनपुत्रियस्य ।
13.29.m: "That face of his in this place" [RV 10.8.5a] is [the offering verse] for the one dedicated to Apāṃ Napāt.
When there are a hundred cows, they let loose a bull among them.
When a thousand are reached, then comes the conclusion;

13.29.s: klākṣam vā prasravaṇam prāpya agnaye kāmāya iṣṭim nirvapanti |
13.29.d: क्लाक्षम् वा प्रस्रवणम् प्राप्य अग्नये कामाय इष्टिम् निर्वपन्ति ।
13.29.m: or, having reached the fountain Plakṣaprāsravaṇa, they offer an iṣṭi to Agni Kāma.

13.29.s: tasyām aśvām ca pauruṣīm ca dhenuke dattvā kāra pacavam prati yamunām avabhṛtham abhyavayanti |
13.29.d: तस्याम् अश्वाम् च पौरुषीम् च धेनुके दत्त्वा कार पचवम् प्रति यमुनाम् अवभृथम् अभ्यवयन्ति ।
13.29.m: At that [iṣṭi], having given a mare and a female slave as milch cows, they go down to the Yamunā at Kārapacava for the purificatory bath.
This is the session of Mitra and Varuṇa.

13.29.s: atirātro abhijid viśvajitau go āyuṣī indra kukṣī atirātraḥ |
13.29.d: अतिरात्रो अभिजिद् विश्वजितौ गो आयुषी इन्द्र कुक्षी अतिरात्रः ।
13.29.m: An Atirātra, the Abhijit and Viśvajit, the Go and Āyus days, the Indra-kukṣi [days], and an Atirātra—

13.29.s: atirātro jyotir gaur āyur viśvajid abhijitāv indra kukṣī atirātraḥ |
13.29.d: अतिरात्रो ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् विश्वजिद् अभिजिताव् इन्द्र कुक्षी अतिरात्रः ।
13.29.m: An Atirātra, the Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyus, Viśvajit and Abhijit, the Indra-kukṣi [days], and an Atirātra—
For a year he should tend the cows of a brahmin.
For a year he should kindle the fire at Vyarṇa Naitaṃdhava.

13.29.s: saṃvatsare parīṇahy agnīn ādhāya dṛṣadvatyā dakṣiṇena tīreṇa āgneyena aṣṭā kapālena śamyā parāse śamyā parāse yajamāna eti |
13.29.d: संवत्सरे परीणह्य् अग्नीन् आधाय दृषद्वत्या दक्षिणेन तीरेण आग्नेयेन अष्टा कपालेन शम्या परासे शम्या परासे यजमान एति ।
13.29.m: After a year, having set up the fires at Parīṇah, along the southern bank of the Dṛṣadvatī, offering an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni at each throw of a yoke-pin, the sacrificer proceeds.

13.29.s: triḥ prakṣām prati yamunām avabhṛtham abhyavayanti |
13.29.d: त्रिः प्रक्षाम् प्रति यमुनाम् अवभृथम् अभ्यवयन्ति ।
13.29.m: Opposite Triplakṣā, they go down to the Yamunā for the purificatory bath.

13.29.s: atirātraḥ sahasram trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarā atirātraḥ prajāpateḥ sahasra saṃvatsaram sahasra saṃvatsaram |
13.29.d: अतिरात्रः सहस्रम् त्रिवृतः संवत्सरा अतिरात्रः प्रजापतेः सहस्र संवत्सरम् सहस्र संवत्सरम् ।
13.29.m: An Atirātra, a thousand Trivṛt years, and an Atirātra are Prajāpati's thousand-year sacrifice, his thousand-year sacrifice.

14.1.m: In one-day sacrifices and Ahīnas, there is modification of the base form.

14.1.s: yasminn ahani yad ahaḥ pradiśyeta savanam vā sahautram tat |
14.1.d: यस्मिन्न् अहनि यद् अहः प्रदिश्येत सवनम् वा सहौत्रम् तत् ।
14.1.m: On whichever day a [particular] day or pressing is prescribed, that carries along its Hotṛ functions.

14.2.s: agny ādheyena brahma varcasa kāmo yajeta |
14.2.d: अग्न्य् आधेयेन ब्रह्म वर्चस कामो यजेत ।
14.2.m: One who desires spiritual lustre should sacrifice with the Agnyādheya [sacrifice].

14.2.s: tasya aṣṭāsv aṣṭāsu stotrāṇi |
14.2.d: तस्य अष्टास्व् अष्टासु स्तोत्राणि ।
14.2.m: Its stotras are in eight [verses] each.

14.2.s: aṣṭa akṣarā gāyatrī |
14.2.d: अष्ट अक्षरा गायत्री ।

14.2.s: tejo brahma varcasam gāyatrī |
14.2.d: तेजो ब्रह्म वर्चसम् गायत्री ।
14.2.m: The Gāyatrī is splendour and spiritual lustre.

14.2.s: rathantaram pṛṣṭham |
14.2.d: रथन्तरम् पृष्ठम् ।

14.2.s: brahma rathantaram |
14.2.d: ब्रह्म रथन्तरम् ।

14.2.s: agniṣṭomo yajñaḥ |
14.2.d: अग्निष्टोमो यज्ञः ।

14.2.s: brahma vā agniṣṭomaḥ |
14.2.d: ब्रह्म वा अग्निष्टोमः ।

14.2.s: etena triḥ samṛddhena brahmaṇā tejo brahma varcasam āpnoti |
14.2.d: एतेन त्रिः समृद्धेन ब्रह्मणा तेजो ब्रह्म वर्चसम् आप्नोति ।
14.2.m: By this threefoldly perfected sacred power, he attains splendour and spiritual lustre.

14.2.s: tṛca klṛptam śastram |
14.2.d: तृच क्लृप्तम् शस्त्रम् ।

14.2.s: trivṛd vā annam annam pānam khādayanti tasya sarvasya āptyai |
14.2.d: त्रिवृद् वा अन्नम् अन्नम् पानम् खादयन्ति तस्य सर्वस्य आप्त्यै ।
14.2.m: Food is threefold: food, drink, and chewable food; [this is] for obtaining all of that.

14.2.s: catur viṃśatir dakṣiṇā |
14.2.d: चतुर् विंशतिर् दक्षिणा ।

14.2.s: catur viṃśatir vai saṃvatsarasya ardha māsāḥ saṃvatsarasya eva āptyai |
14.2.d: चतुर् विंशतिर् वै संवत्सरस्य अर्ध मासाः संवत्सरस्य एव आप्त्यै ।
14.2.m: Twenty-four indeed are the half-months of the year; [this is] just for obtaining the year.

14.2.s: tasya agnaye pavamānāya pāvakāya śucaya iti paśava upālambhyāḥ savanīyasya |
14.2.d: तस्य अग्नये पवमानाय पावकाय शुचय इति पशव उपालम्भ्याः सवनीयस्य ।
14.2.m: For it, animals to Agni Pavamāna, to Pāvaka, [and] to Śuci are to be seized in place of the savanīya animal.

14.2.s: ādityā vaśā anubandhyāyā upālambhya evam vidhā |
14.2.d: आदित्या वशा अनुबन्ध्याया उपालम्भ्य एवम् विधा ।
14.2.m: A barren cow to Aditi is to be seized in place of the subsequently bound victim of this kind.

14.2.s: tad yad evam paśavo niyuktā bhavanti na id agny ādheyād ayāni iti |
14.2.d: तद् यद् एवम् पशवो नियुक्ता भवन्ति न इद् अग्न्य् आधेयाद् अयानि इति ।
14.2.m: The reason why the animals are bound thus is: 'Lest I depart from the establishment of the fires'.

14.2.s: tasya prātaḥ savanīyān anu puroḷāśān agnaye pavamānāya aṣṭa kapālam puroḷāśam nirvapati |
14.2.d: तस्य प्रातः सवनीयान् अनु पुरोऌआशान् अग्नये पवमानाय अष्ट कपालम् पुरोऌआशम् निर्वपति ।
14.2.m: For it, following the morning-pressing sacrificial cakes, he offers an eight-pot-sherd sacrificial cake to Agni Pavamāna.

14.2.s: mādhyaṃdinīyān anu puroḷāśān agnaye pāvakasya |
14.2.d: माध्यंदिनीयान् अनु पुरोऌआशान् अग्नये पावकस्य ।
14.2.m: Following the midday-pressing sacrificial cakes, [he offers one] to Agni Pāvaka.

14.2.s: tṛtīya savanīyān anu puroḷāśān agnaye śucaye |
14.2.d: तृतीय सवनीयान् अनु पुरोऌआशान् अग्नये शुचये ।
14.2.m: Following the third-pressing sacrificial cakes, [he offers one] to Agni Śuci.

14.2.s: āvapanam vai savanīyāḥ puroḷāśāḥ | āvapana eva tad āvapati |
14.2.d: आवपनम् वै सवनीयाः पुरोऌआशाः । आवपन एव तद् आवपति ।
14.2.m: The savanīya sacrificial cakes are indeed an insertion; he inserts that into the very insertion.

14.2.s: atha yad ādityā vaśā anubandhyāyā upālambhyā bhavaty aditim vā anvagny ādheyam saṃtiṣṭhate |
14.2.d: अथ यद् आदित्या वशा अनुबन्ध्याया उपालम्भ्या भवत्य् अदितिम् वा अन्वग्न्य् आधेयम् संतिष्ठते ।
14.2.m: Now, as to why a barren cow to Aditi is to be seized in place of the subsequently bound victim: the establishment of the fires concludes along with Aditi.

14.2.s: yā anvagny ādheyasya saṃsthā tām eva tad yajñasya saṃsthām karoti |
14.2.d: या अन्वग्न्य् आधेयस्य संस्था ताम् एव तद् यज्ञस्य संस्थाम् करोति ।
14.2.m: Whatever is the conclusion of the establishment of the fires, he thereby makes that very conclusion for the sacrifice.
